content: 1. When using fostemsavir with a BCRP inhibitor, it is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. For example, fostemsavir should not be co-administered with betibeglogene autotemcel. Antiretroviral medications should not be taken for at least one month before stem cell mobilization or during the expected duration of medication elimination, and until all apheresis cycles are completed. This is because antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. 2. Bosentan is contraindicated with fostemsavir as it decreases fostemsavir levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, fostemsavir increases bosentan levels. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored due to fostemsavir's inhibition of OATP1B1/3 transporters. If possible, avoid co-administration or adjust the dose of OATP1B1/3 substrates. 3. Both bosutinib and fostemsavir increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 4. Buprenorphine (in all forms: buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection) and fostemsavir both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Butabarbital and butalbital are contraindicated with fostemsavir as they decrease fostemsavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduces the active moiety (temsavir) plasma concentrations, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. 6. Capecitabine and fostemsavir both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 7.
